questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city and country itself, I had long wanted to live in Edinburgh city since I last visited it. The university was also fairly well known as a good university which sealed the deal for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. The exchange student office at Edinburgh University is very helpful and answers questions quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh sent me check lists of what things I needed to do in order to confirm and check in at Edinburgh University. Furthermore, welcome week offered loads of events to meet new people both inside and outside your study.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult - Edinburgh is currently experiencing a housing crisis which meant that I spent many hours to find a place to live. Because I am postgraduate and an international student I was not guaranteed student housing. I found private housing using the app "Spareroom" which was fairly easy to use, and felt safer from housing scams than facebook. However, be aware that you can still be scammed through housing-apps such as Spareroom, so be careful. I was offered student accommodation a week before I was supposed to travel to Edinburgh, but at that point I had already found a private room - so be aware that Edinburgh might offer you student accommodation really late - however if you're a postgraduate exchange student, dont count on it and look for private accommodation simultanously.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: if you live far enough away from campus that you have to take the bus, be aware that the bus-system is so-so. While there are many busstops and lines which can bring you wherever you want to go, the busses can be a bit unreliable (not too bad tho). This is (propably) due to the fact that Edinburgh has a lot of traffic, which delays the busses. However it was not impossible, and I used the bus-system everyday without it disturbing my daily goings too much - it was more of an annoyance than a real issue. However, I would recommend trying to find a place that is walking distance from South Bridge, which is the meeting spot for a lot of students - many student accommodations are situated close by and a lot of pubs and clubs are in this area as well. It is possible to get a bus home at night, but again be prepared that they might be a bit late or not show up at all.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy and very clearly communicated

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They send you an email welcoming you and tells you to show up for "international check-in", which is basicly where you show up with your passport and they confirm your attendance. Then, you also do a check-in at your particular study, and then your done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the office for exchange students, which is how I asked for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of my classes I didnt get, but I was generally happy with the course that replaced it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get it over with fast, it doesnt take long.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: MA courses were very focused on class discussions which made them engaging and challenging without being too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: fairly similar, however the classes were smaller at Edinburgh, some classes we were only 10 people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender, politics and representation
The Middle East in International relations
Survey in the Middle Eastern Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the two Middle Eastern classes, even though I had never taken a class of the middle east before they were still fairly introducory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was more exspensive than expected, however I found something fairly cheap compared to other places - in general be expected to pay between 6000-9000 kroner for a room.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cost of living in Edinburgh is less costly than Copenhagen, so eating out at restaurants and cafés, going for drinks and buying groceries were generally 20-25 pct cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Edinburgh has an amazing student life, with student societies for almost anything you can think of: fitness, sports, crafts, partying, hobbies, politics, languages, you name it! I really recommend joining one or two societies.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again almost anything you can think off is a society at Edinburgh University, and they all create events - sometimes the events are open to non-members, other times you have to be a member of the society to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The wine society was really fun and a great way to get to know new people. If your into sports, I also recommend joining one of their sports-societies, which is student-led but still very high-quality (and good for the price!).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: A lot of museums is free in Edinburgh, so I recommend that. Also going on a weekend-trip to the highlands is a must, I personally went to Isle of Skye, which was absolutely stunning. Scotland has some of the most beautiful nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, its quite similar to danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in welcome week and join a society, people are very eager to make new friends. Join the Erasmus students group chat, its very active during the first couple of week with people looking to meet new people. Welcome week can be quite overwhelming, there like 20 events everyday, but choose a couple each day and dont worry about missing some of them - you cant make them all!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didnt really find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pub-culture is amazing in Edinburgh, generally the night-life is very lively and people are very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start early (but not too early) when finding housing. I started 2 months before, but my search really began around 1,5-1 month before my move-in date, because most rooms are only offered or rented out a month in advance. Apply for student housing at the university even if they tell you its not guaranteed - you might just be offered something anyway! 

Join a society - Its a great way to get to know new people, and there really is something for everyone. 

Be patient - Edinburgh University is generally really late in confirming your exchange. I got my final confirmation that I had been accepted as an exchange student from Edinburgh University in late July, and the semester starts september 11th! So if you haven't heard from UED, dont panic, they are generally late in confirming their students attendance.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are not many study-seats at the libraries, so remember to get up early during exam period if you want a seat at the library - or sit at a cafe.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social aspect of EUD, they have one of the most well-developed student-led social scene I have ever experienced.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Transportation to and from campus via bus- It wasn't a huge problem, but the buses are often 10-15 min late which can be a bit annoying.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
